title: May They Be Blessed
subtitle: Whether child or lamb, they still deserve deliverance.

trails.title: 20th Century Miracles
trails.description: Details a significant event of the late 20th century. Essential reading.

content.text:
Methods

Through the aid of voluntary donations, the research team extracted a nucleus from a female arcanist (Genetic Mother A) and an enucleated egg cell from a female human (Genetic Mother B). The nucleus was cultivated and processed to enhance its receptivity to new genetic instructions. After injecting the donor cell nucleus into the enucleated egg cell, an electric pulse was used to fuse the nucleus with the egg cytoplasm, initiating cell division and forming embryonic cells. During this process, the ratio of arcanist to human genetic material was adjusted to be nearly equal.

In Experiment No. 277, the embryo developed well, meeting the criteria for transplantation, and was implanted into the uterus of a Finn-Dorset ewe after formation.

Observations

0 Months Old

The subject was born through natural delivery, with 60.05% arcanist genetic material and 39.95% human genetic material, not achieving the expected complete balance, but still proving that the adult somatic cells of an arcanist can be programmed and adjusted through cloning technology.

In appearance, the subject exhibits characteristics of both Genetic Mothers A and B; simultaneously, for unknown reasons, its head is highly similar to that of a Finn-Dorset, but brain development has not been affected.

2 Months Old

The subject's development is slower than that of contemporary human and arcanist infants. Mild symptoms of lung infection have been found.

4 Months Old

The subject's development is slower than that of contemporary human and arcanist infants, but it showed significant responses to music and human language, with consistent reactions to specific sounds.

The cause of the lung infection was identified; the subject's lungs tested positive for the JSRV retrovirus, commonly found in sheep living indoors for extended periods. It was suggested that a veterinary team be brought in for consultation.

6 Months Old

The subject's physical development is slower than that of contemporary human and arcanist infants, and may stop developing prematurely.

Sterile room staff reported that the subject began consciously mimicking communication behaviors, as expected. Educational classes and moral guidance videotapes were initiated.

The lung infection worsened, and the subject showed a strong allergic reaction to chemical fiber products.

...

10 Months Old

The subject can engage in rudimentary communication, exhibiting good brain development.

Multiple tests have confirmed that American country music is effective in alleviating the subject's allergic reactions, the cause of which is yet to be determined.
...

22 Months Old

The subject performed excellently in communication and intelligence tests, possessing the intelligence level of a 7-year-old human child.

23 Months Old

Bone tests indicated that the subject's physical development will cease completely by the age of 12.

items.text: The voice on the other end continues.

items.speaker: Barbara
items.text: Wonderful, I can talk over the phone now. The wind must still be wandering nearby.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: That's good to hear.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Are you an editor for UTTU?
There's a sigh of relief.

items.speaker: Barbara
items.text: Yes, Miss, I am.

items.speaker: Barbara
items.text: But before we continue our conversation, could you please tell me what year it is now?

items.speaker: Barbara
items.text: I see.
The frail voice steadies.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Ms. Barbara, can I meet you in person?

items.speaker: Barbara
items.text: You want to meet me?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Yes, I'm Vertin, the Timekeeper of the St. Pavlov Foundation. I was sent to ask you about Urd's whereabouts.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: But you don't seem to be in a favorable situation right now.

items.speaker: Barbara
items.text: Ms. Vertin, I couldn't possibly locate Urd's whereabouts. The whispers of the wind can't reach this room.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: The whispers of the wind?

items.speaker: Barbara
items.text: Yes, it's a special form of communication.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Right. Well, is there anything I can do to help you rebuild this line of communication?

items.speaker: Barbara
items.text: Hmm. Let me first explain the situation to you. Here are a few things I'm certain of:

items.speaker: Barbara
items.text: First, this isn't an ordinary motel. It possesses some kind of supernatural life force.

items.speaker: Barbara
items.text: Before checking in, I interviewed some of the residents nearby. They all mentioned eerie rumors centered around the motel these past few months.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Yes, we've encountered some bizarre events here. Like real-life urban legends.

items.speaker: Barbara
items.text: Second, I'm now trapped in a red room.

items.speaker: Barbara
items.text: This room is in the same motel as yours. What's different is that it blocks all forms of communication.

items.speaker: Barbara
items.text: I couldn't get the room to open, and my voice didn't reach through the phone.

items.speaker: Barbara
items.text: That was until a gunshot broke this intangible restraint. This small room contracted violently, and now I can communicate with the outside world.

items.speaker: Barbara
items.text: At first, I thought it was an earthquake, but the contracted space soon returned to normal. Earthquakes can't do that, can they?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Before this happened, were you using spiders to communicate with the world outside?

items.speaker: Barbara
items.text: Yes, I was. As luck would have it, there are many spiders here. Thanks to the prevalence of spiders in urban legends, I assume.
They can hear the sound of pages being turned from the other end of the telephone.

items.speaker: Barbara
items.text: There's some paranoia about "spiders living in hair." It originated in a sermon from 13th-century England.

items.speaker: Barbara
items.text: A woman was always late to mass because she spent too much time styling her hair. Eventually, a devil attached itself to her hair in the form of a spider.

items.speaker: Barbara
items.text: Yes, they delivered messages for me in their own peculiar way.

items.speaker: Barbara
items.text: Being completely isolated from the outside world greatly unsettled me. It reminded me of that terrible phenomenon.
She takes a few light breaths.

items.speaker: Barbara
items.text: Fortunately, that wasn't the case.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: But you're still trapped in that room, right?

items.speaker: Barbara
items.text: Yes. The door's gone. I can't get out from the inside.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: How did you get in there in the first place? Or rather, who brought you into that room?

items.speaker: Barbara
items.text: Well, who else could it be?

items.speaker: Barbara
items.text: The maid named Tuesday.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Just as I expected.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Wait.
The mercenary cuts in.

items.speaker: Barbara
items.text: You're that driver who left me on the road, right? I remember your voice.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Yeah, it's me.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: I actually changed my mind and turned back to get you, but you were gone by the time I arrived.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: I guess that's when you came to this motel, right?

items.speaker: Barbara
items.text: Yes, Tuesday saw me and invited me here.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Oh.

items.speaker: Barbara
items.text: Did you wanna ask me something?

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Have you seen a girl of about 5 foot 3 here?

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: In a white dress. Curly chestnut-colored hair. Green eyes. Small hands.

items.speaker: Barbara
items.text: I may have seen her.

items.speaker: Barbara
items.text: When I first arrived, I saw a girl who matched your description coming down the hallway.

items.speaker: Barbara
items.text: She was carrying an empty basket. I presumed that she'd been shopping in the town nearby.

items.speaker: Barbara
items.text: If I recall correctly, she didn't check out.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Thank you.
She slumps her shoulders, and the light in her eye dims.
She says no more.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: How can we find this room?

items.speaker: Barbara
items.text: It's just in the hallway, number 707.

items.speaker: Barbara
items.text: Look for a door covered in red—
*beep—beep—beep*

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Looks like the phone got disconnected.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: So Barbara's in that room that Stefen saw. Number 707.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I'm going to find it. What about you? Heading into town for Kayla?
After a brief silence, Argus speaks.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: I did notice a weird spot in the hallway earlier. The maid's footprints were going back and forth, like there was an entrance there.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: But I didn't see no signs of a door.
She scratches her head with the barrel of her gun.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I wouldn't be surprised if you died by your own gun one day.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Haha, that'd be a memorable way to go.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Alright, enough kidding around.
She perks up.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Our Little Miss Maid tried so very hard to hide Barbara from us, but I guess the lamb's out of the bag now.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Yes. It's all crystal clear now. Let's go.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Hold up a sec, boss.
She bites her lip.

items.speaker: Argus
items.text: Do you have any candies? I'm running on fumes here, and I ain't got no way to replenish my stash.
Asking for help seems very difficult for her.
She pulls a few pieces of candy from her pocket and places them in Argus's palm.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Us and Barbara will be out of here soon.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: And you'll find some candy and Kayla in town.
